teams.heading: Jake White names Ikanivere-led Fiji XV with Volavola and Lomani at half-back
teams.body: Fiji head coach Jake White has made hooker Tevita Ikanivere captain for Saturday's Nations Championship test against Italy in Udine. Frank Lomani is at scrum-half and Ben Volavola, listed without a club, is at fly-half. Nathan Hughes starts at No. 8 and Josua Tuisova at inside centre, with Caleb Muntz among the replacements. Fiji are bottom of their pool without a point after last week's 15-43 defeat by Ireland in Dublin. They face a sixth-place play-off against Italy at Twickenham if they lose or win without a bonus point.

lead.why: Jake White's team announcement is the day's fresh Fiji event; the other new items are Italy's selection and Quesada's comments.

teams.heading: Steve Borthwick backs referees but declines to condemn Rassie Erasmus's claims
teams.body: England head coach Steve Borthwick would not address claims by Springbok head coach Rassie Erasmus, banned for six matches by World Rugby, that referee Andrea Piardi and his assistants had shown France leniency. Instead, he urged respect for referees: "I have absolute 100% confidence and faith that every match official in every game tries to do the very best they can." Naming his side for Saturday's All Blacks test, Borthwick also backed RFU referee Christophe Ridley, a regular at England's camp, for South Africa v Ireland.

lead.why: A fresh Borthwick press-room stance on the week's biggest row, and not yet covered on this tab.

teams.heading: Rugbyrama review backs France's knee-down tackling after Rassie Erasmus's illegality claim
teams.body: Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus branded France's knee-to-ground tackles in last weekend's 21-19 win illegal, but Rugbyrama's review of the match finds most were made with the knee landing at the moment of impact — which keeps them legal. France have drilled the technique for several years under William Servat, their contact-skills coach, to bring tackle height down. Erasmus has been handed a six-week suspension, and Rugbyrama notes it remains to be seen how referees will read the confusion he has sown, ahead of Saturday's test against Argentina.

lead.why: The selection story has already run, and this is the freshest distinct France story: a review defending the Bleus' tackling after Erasmus's illegality charge.

teams.heading: Hugo Keenan to win 50th Ireland cap at full-back against Springboks
teams.body: Ireland full-back Hugo Keenan brings up his half-century of caps in Saturday's Nations Championship Test against world champions South Africa, Planet Rugby reports. Head coach Andy Farrell names Robert Baloucoune and Mack Hansen on the wings, with Stuart McCloskey and Robbie Henshaw linking up again in midfield and Sam Prendergast partnering Jamison Gibson-Park at half-back. Captain Dan Sheehan, back from concussion, starts at No. 8. The42 reports the Springboks remain 10-point favourites for the game in Dublin.

lead.why: Sheehan at No. 8 has already been read, so Keenan's 50th cap in the confirmed team is the freshest Ireland selection story.

teams.heading: Domingo Miotti says joking message to Quesada started his road to Italy
teams.body: Italy fly-half Domingo Miotti, who wins his first cap against Fiji in Udine on Saturday, says his switch began with a congratulatory message to Gonzalo Quesada when his former Jaguares coach became Italy head coach, adding in jest that he had an Italian grandfather. Miotti, whose maternal grandfather was from Lucca, said the idea turned serious over the past year before he raised it with Quesada again this summer. Americas Rugby News reports he turned down a July recall from Argentina head coach Felipe Contepomi to stay eligible.

lead.why: Miotti's account of how his Italy switch began is new, Italy-centred and distinct from yesterday's selection story.

teams.heading: Japan coach Eddie Jones says Scotland should be grateful for Gregor Townsend
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones used the build-up to Saturday's Nations Championship visit to Murrayfield to back Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend, nine and a half years into the job. "To do 10 years in charge at a top-eight team in the world is a great accomplishment," Jones told BBC Sport, arguing that a country with two professional teams has been knocking on the door of the top four. As England coach, Jones got the better of Townsend only once in five Six Nations meetings.

lead.why: A fresh, on-the-record verdict on Townsend's tenure from the opposing coach on the eve of the test.

teams.heading: Dan Edwards ankle injury in training sees Wales call up Jarrod Evans
teams.body: Ospreys playmaker Dan Edwards suffered an ankle injury in training this week, and Cardiff's Jarrod Evans has been called into the wider Nations Championship squad, the WRU confirmed. Edwards' place in the matchday squad for Saturday's test against Australia at Principality Stadium goes to Scarlets centre or fly-half Joe Hawkins, named at No. 22. Lock Adam Beard is also missing with a shoulder injury suffered against New Zealand, so Taine Plumtree covers the second row from the bench.

lead.why: A fresh Wales injury and squad call-up is a reported event the reader hasn't seen, unlike the already-covered recalls and the Botham omission.

teams.heading: Pumas face Galthié's overhauled France back row with Jalibert recalled at fly-half
teams.body: France head coach Fabien Galthié has changed his entire back row for Saturday's test against Argentina at the Stade de France. Rugbyrama reports that Charles Ollivon, Anthony Jelonch and Esteban Capilla start, with Grégory Alldritt and Cameron Woki dropping to the bench. Bordeaux-Bègles fly-half Matthieu Jalibert starts at No. 10 in his first outing of any kind since September after injury, Planet Rugby notes, relegating Maxime Lucu to the replacements. France top the northern pool and are chasing next week's final at Twickenham.

lead.why: Montoya's return has already run, so the freshest Pumas-relevant event is France naming a rebuilt back row and a returning fly-half to face them.

teams.heading: Rugby Australia farewells Dean Duncan, former Lloyd McDermott Rugby Development Team president
teams.body: The proud Kamilaroi man, who died of acute myeloid leukaemia last month, has been honoured at St Francis Xavier Church and buried at Moree Lawn Cemetery. Beyond the Lloydies, Duncan sat on Rugby Australia's Diversity Council and First Nations Rugby Committee and delivered countless cultural gift presentations to national and visiting teams. He was with the Wallabies for NAIDOC Week in Melbourne in 2024. The tributes come as head coach Les Kiss's side prepare to face Wales in Cardiff on Saturday.

lead.why: The McReight selection story has already run, so the freshest new Australia item is Rugby Australia's tribute to Dean Duncan.

teams.heading: Japan without centre Dylan Riley for personal reasons against Scotland at Murrayfield
teams.body: Rugby Asia 247 reports that Dylan Riley, described as Japan's centre lynchpin, misses Saturday's Nations Championship pool finale against Scotland at Murrayfield for personal reasons. Shuhei Takeuchi, Riku Tokito and props Keijiro Tamafusa and Opeti Helu are also out through injury or condition. Japan, beaten 78-15 by England last week, have called up Toyota Verblitz pair Taufa Latu and Nicholas McCullan and Kubota Spears Funabashi/Tokyo Bay's Halatoa Vailea.

lead.why: Riley's absence and the injury list are a Japan availability story distinct from the selection already reported.

teams.heading: Sir Steve Hansen says Wales loss will help Rennie's All Blacks improve
teams.body: Former All Blacks head coach Sir Steve Hansen insists New Zealand are improving under current coach Dave Rennie despite last Saturday's 28-35 defeat to Wales — their first in 73 years. Asked on the For The Love Of Rugby podcast whether the side are heading in the right direction, Hansen cited clarity, unity and joy, adding: "Funnily enough, I think the loss against Wales will actually help them get better." He also called the fly-half depth, with Damian McKenzie replacing Richie Mo'unga for Saturday's England test, a luxury worth keeping.

lead.why: The team announcement has already run, so Hansen's backing of Rennie after the Wales defeat is the freshest New Zealand story.

teams.heading: Springboks to face Rónan Kelleher, not Dan Sheehan, at scrum in Dublin
teams.body: Ireland head coach Andy Farrell has moved Dan Sheehan from hooker to No. 8 for Saturday's Nations Championship test at the Aviva Stadium, handing the No. 2 shirt to Rónan Kelleher. The42 notes that the Springboks relentlessly attacked Sheehan at scrum time last year. It reads the switch as Farrell and Ireland scrum coach John Fogarty hoping that Kelleher, rated Ireland's best scrummaging hooker, fares better against the Bok scrum. With both sides named, the outlet still has South Africa as 10-point favourites.

lead.why: Both teams are now named, and Ireland's hooker switch goes straight at the Springbok scrum that targeted Sheehan last year.
